---
title: "Projected change of thermal indices: WorldClim CMIP6"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, dpi = 96,
                      out.width = "100%")
library(thermify)
province <- read.csv("data/cc-cauquenes-province.csv")
stations_cc <- read.csv("data/cc-ceaza-stations.csv")
stations <- read.csv("data/ceaza-stations.csv", encoding = "UTF-8")
index_label <- c(gdd = "Degree-days (base 10 degC)",
                 ch = "Chilling hours (0-7.2 degC)", cu = "Utah chill units",
                 cp = "Chill portions (Dynamic)")
unit <- c(gdd = "degC day", ch = "h", cu = "units", cp = "portions")
ssp_label <- c("245" = "SSP2-4.5", "585" = "SSP5-8.5")
```

How much would degree-days and winter chill change by mid-century? This page
uses the WorldClim 2.1 downscaled CMIP6 projections, read with
`worldclim_future_region()`, for **14 global climate models (GCMs)**, two
scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5) and the period **2041-2060**, against the
WorldClim 1970-2000 baseline.

> **Read these numbers as changes, not as future values.** The validation
> with observed stations
> ([CEAZA-Met article](validation-ceaza.html)) showed that WorldClim and
> monthly climatologies have large errors for chill, so this page reports
> the **change** between the future and the baseline of the same data,
> where much of that error cancels. It also reports the spread between
> models: a single GCM can be far from the consensus.

Scripts: `data-raw/climate-change/`. Heat season 1 September - 30 April;
chill season 1 May - 31 August.

## Province of Cauquenes (Maule)

Indices computed with `thermify_rast()` from the monthly WorldClim surfaces
(degree-days with the averaging method; chill with the Linvill hourly
reconstruction, `ch_methods = "hourly"`).

```{r province-table}
base <- province[province$ssp == "baseline", ]
rows <- list()
for (s in c("245", "585")) for (ix in names(index_label)) {
  b <- base$value[base$index == ix]
  d <- province$value[province$ssp == s & province$index == ix] - b
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    Scenario = ssp_label[[s]], Index = index_label[[ix]],
    Baseline = sprintf("%.0f %s", b, unit[[ix]]),
    `Median change` = sprintf("%+.0f (%+.0f %%)", stats::median(d),
                              100 * stats::median(d) / b),
    `Range of 14 GCMs` = sprintf("%+.0f to %+.0f", min(d), max(d)),
    check.names = FALSE)
}
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, rows), row.names = FALSE, caption = paste(
  "Province mean, 2041-2060 against 1970-2000. Baselines are WorldClim",
  "values and inherit their errors; use the changes."))
```

```{r maps, fig.height = 7}
prov <- cauquenes_boundary("provincia", crs = "EPSG:4326")
ix_show <- c("gdd", "ch", "cp")
pal <- list(gdd = grDevices::hcl.colors(30, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE),
            ch = grDevices::hcl.colors(30, "Blues", rev = FALSE),
            cp = grDevices::hcl.colors(30, "Blues", rev = FALSE))
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 5))
for (s in c("245", "585")) for (ix in ix_show) {
  r <- terra::rast(sprintf("data/cc-cauquenes-%s-ssp%s.tif", ix, s))
  rng <- range(unlist(lapply(c("245", "585"), function(ss) {
    terra::minmax(terra::rast(sprintf("data/cc-cauquenes-%s-ssp%s.tif",
                                      ix, ss))[["median_change"]])
  })))
  terra::plot(r[["median_change"]], col = pal[[ix]], range = rng,
              axes = FALSE, mar = c(1, 1, 3, 5),
              main = sprintf("%s\n%s (%s)", ssp_label[[s]],
                             sub(" \\(.*", "", index_label[[ix]]),
                             unit[[ix]]), cex.main = 0.95)
  terra::lines(prov)
}
par(op)
```

Median change across the 14 GCMs, 2041-2060. For degree-days, chilling
hours and Utah units all 14 models agree on the sign of the change in every
cell. For chill portions they do not everywhere: in the coldest fifth of the
province (winter mean temperature of about 6-8 degrees C) the median change
is close to zero, sometimes slightly positive, and the models split; in the
rest every model projects a loss, larger where winters are milder. This is
expected from the Dynamic model, in which chill accumulates most efficiently
at moderate temperatures: a cold site can lose little chill, or even gain
some, from a moderate warming.

### The choice of chill model changes the conclusion

Under the same warming, **chilling hours fall by about half, but chill
portions fall by less than a tenth**. Chilling hours count every hour
between 0 and 7.2 degrees C and ignore that slightly warmer hours still
contribute to chill accumulation; the Dynamic model, which describes chill
accumulation and its reversal by heat, responds much less to a moderate
warming. Studies that report future chill only as chilling hours therefore
tend to overstate the loss (Luedeling et al. 2011). For planning,
**prefer chill portions**, and report chilling hours only for comparison
with older literature.

## CEAZA-Met stations (north-central Chile): delta method

At 29 of the 30 stations of the [validation](validation-ceaza.html), each model's
monthly change at the station's WorldClim cell (future minus 1970-2000) is
applied to **every hour of the station's observed record**: the shift goes
from the change of the minimum at the daily minimum to the change of the
maximum at the daily maximum. The indices are then computed from the
modified hourly series, season by season, exactly as the reference of the
validation. This keeps the observed day-to-day and year-to-year variability,
and the present-day baseline is the observed index. Punta de Choros is
excluded: the station is on the shoreline and its WorldClim cell is sea
(no data), so there is no model change to apply.

A simpler variant, adding the change to the station's monthly climatology,
is **not** used: monthly climatologies lose the cold nights, give zero chill
portions at several interior stations that actually accumulate 27-31
portions per season, and make marginal sites lose all their chill under any
warming.

```{r stations, fig.height = 5}
st <- merge(stations_cc, stations, by = "station")
gcm_median <- stats::aggregate(
  cbind(baseline, change) ~ station + name + elevation + ssp + index,
  data = st, FUN = stats::median)
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
for (ix in c("gdd", "cp")) {
  d <- gcm_median[gcm_median$index == ix, ]
  rel <- ifelse(abs(d$baseline) > 1e-9, 100 * d$change / d$baseline, NA)
  cols <- ifelse(d$ssp == 245, "#0B5563", "#E8702A")
  plot(d$elevation, rel, pch = 21, bg = adjustcolor(cols, 0.75),
       col = "white", cex = 1.3, las = 1, xlab = "Station elevation (m)",
       ylab = "Median relative change (%)", main = index_label[[ix]],
       cex.main = 0.95)
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey50")
  legend(if (ix == "gdd") "topright" else "bottomright",
         legend = ssp_label, pt.bg = c("#0B5563", "#E8702A"), pch = 21,
         col = "white", pt.cex = 1.3, bty = "n")
}
par(op)
```

Each point is a station and scenario (median of the 14 GCMs).

```{r stations-table}
d <- gcm_median
d$rel <- ifelse(abs(d$baseline) > 1e-9, 100 * d$change / d$baseline, NA)
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("245", "585"), function(s) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(index_label), function(ix) {
    x <- d[d$ssp == as.integer(s) & d$index == ix, ]
    data.frame(Scenario = ssp_label[[s]], Index = index_label[[ix]],
               `Median over stations` = sprintf("%+.0f %%",
                 stats::median(x$rel, na.rm = TRUE)),
               `Stations losing all chill` = if (ix == "gdd") "-" else
                 as.character(sum(x$baseline > 0 & x$baseline + x$change <= 0)),
               check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}))
warm <- stats::aggregate(cbind(delta_tmin, delta_tmax) ~ ssp,
                         data = stations_cc, FUN = stats::median)
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, caption = sprintf(paste(
  "Median relative change over the stations (each station: median of 14",
  "GCMs). Median warming at the stations: SSP2-4.5 %+.1f degC (Tmin) and",
  "%+.1f degC (Tmax); SSP5-8.5 %+.1f and %+.1f degC."),
  warm$delta_tmin[warm$ssp == 245], warm$delta_tmax[warm$ssp == 245],
  warm$delta_tmin[warm$ssp == 585], warm$delta_tmax[warm$ssp == 585]))
```

With a similar warming at the stations (about +1.9 degrees C under SSP2-4.5),
the semi-arid north loses a much larger share of its chill than Cauquenes:
the median station loses about **a third of its chill portions** (37 % under
SSP2-4.5, 42 % under SSP5-8.5), against less than a tenth in Cauquenes. The
losses are largest on the coast (about two thirds at Caleta El Toro, La
Serena and Coquimbo, below 130 m) and smallest at the highest station
(about 10 % at Los Molles, 2,543 m). No station loses all its chill
portions. Chilling hours, which already fall by about half at the median
station, disappear at the coastal stations whose baseline is only 2-13 hours per
season (two stations under SSP2-4.5, three under SSP5-8.5). Utah units can be negative because the Utah model
subtracts chill for warm hours, so their relative changes are unstable near
zero and exceed -100 % at some stations; use them with care in mild
climates.

## Limitations

* **Changes, not forecasts.** WorldClim future surfaces add each model's
  change to the 1970-2000 baseline; the results describe a climate
  centred on 2041-2060, not any particular year.
* **Monthly data in Cauquenes.** The province maps are computed from
  monthly climatologies, which lose day-to-day variability and bias absolute
  chill values (about -25 % for chilling hours in the validation); changes
  are less affected but not immune. The station analysis avoids this by
  using the observed hourly records, but assumes that day-to-day and
  diurnal variability stay as they are.
* **Model spread.** The table shows the range of 14 GCMs; some (for
  example CanESM5 and UKESM1-0-LL) warm more than most models. The median
  is the summary to use.
* **Baseline period.** The baseline is 1970-2000; part of the projected
  change has already happened.
* **Validation.** Chill estimates have been validated only in semi-arid
  north-central Chile; the central-south is pending.

## References

Luedeling, E., Girvetz, E. H., Semenov, M. A., & Brown, P. H. (2011).
Climate change affects winter chill for temperate fruit and nut trees.
*PLoS ONE*, 6(5), e20155. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0020155>

Fick, S. E., & Hijmans, R. J. (2017). WorldClim 2: new 1-km spatial
resolution climate surfaces for global land areas. *International Journal
of Climatology*, 37(12), 4302-4315. <https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.5086>
